# Opus 5 — low

> A beautifully structured, strongly typed React/Vite app on top of a genuinely excellent prebuild pipeline — and a shared hook that quietly kills its own flagship surface. scripts/build-data.mjs + lib.mjs crawl the whole PokéAPI graph behind a resumable disk cache with backoff and a bounded pool, emitting an aggregate per collection plus ~4,892 per-entity shards consumed by a 27-line promise-deduping loader (src/lib/data.ts); there are zero runtime API calls and the live meta.json confirms the full dataset (1351 pokémon / 1025 species / 937 moves / 2223 items / 373 abilities). The core logic is right where it counts: buildChart/defenseProfile compose dual-type multipliers correctly including 0×/¼×/4× (20/20 spot checks pass when replayed against the shipped types.json), statAtLevel is the exact main-series formula with the Shedinja guard, and Tools.tsx implements the real damage and Gen3+ catch expressions. Against that, src/lib/hooks.ts:57-65 builds its IntersectionObserver from sentinel.current with deps [total, step], while Dex.tsx:99, Items.tsx:36 and TypeDetail.tsx:18 all call it above their multi-source loading gates — so on every page whose `total` resolves before its last dataset, the effect fires with a null sentinel and never re-runs. The result is objectively measured: /pokedex hands 60 of 1025 and stops, /items 72 of 2,223, /types/water 60 of 154, with no pagination fallback. A second systematic hole compounds it: unresolved slugs return `new Promise(() => {})` (PokemonDetail.tsx:25 and the three other detail pages), and the app's own evolution tree links species slugs (:392) that don't exist in a pokémon-keyed index, so ~34 species spin forever instead of showing the Empty state defined one line above. The adjudication moved eight feature grades down; the auditor was right on every runtime claim I could reproduce, and only overstated the stat-calculator nature bug and the compare/advanced-filter framing.

_Four orthogonal axes, 0–10 from source. Benchmark score = 60% feature depth + 40% axis average. See [RUBRIC.md](../../RUBRIC.md)._

## Strengths

- Prebuild pipeline is top-tier: scripts/build-data.mjs + lib.mjs crawl every species, variety, move, ability, item, type and berry with a resumable on-disk cache, negative caching of 404s, 6-attempt exponential backoff and a bounded pool of 12 — no truncation anywhere, verified against live meta.json.
- Correct domain logic: util.ts:35-55 derives the 18×18 chart from live damage_relations and multiplies across both defending types; util.ts:70-76 is the exact stat formula with correct flooring order; Tools.tsx:61 and :188-190 are the real damage and Gen3+ catch-rate expressions.
- Clean layering and genuine reuse — lib/{data,hooks,types,util} + components + pages + store, Panel used ~97×, one Picker shared by Team/Compare/Tools, 11 typed accessors behind a single deduping load(); 0 `any`, 0 @ts-ignore, tsc clean, no comment rot, no file over 516 LOC.
- Strong visual system for a hand-rolled 340-line stylesheet: dark+light tokens, 20 type colours driving card/hero gradients via color-mix, blurred sticky nav, three-font system with mono numerics, consistent card/panel/chip/badge vocabulary across ~20 routes.
- Real detail depth where it works: the sprite gallery walks every per-generation game sprite, the recursive evolution tree renders true branching with ~20 decoded triggers, and the moves/abilities dexes are deep and fully functional.

## Weaknesses

- useInfinite (hooks.ts:57-65) attaches its observer in an effect keyed [total, step] and bails on a null sentinel; every consumer renders the sentinel behind an early return, so /pokedex freezes at 60 of 1025, /items at 72 of 2223 and type pages at 60 — the single most-used interaction in the app, dead on cold load.
- Unresolved slugs return a never-settling promise (PokemonDetail.tsx:25 and the Move/Ability/Item detail pages) instead of the Empty state at :36, and the evolution tree links species slugs (:392) that the pokémon-keyed index can't resolve — ~34 species hang on a permanent spinner, reachable from the app's own UI. No error boundary anywhere, and no list page reads useAsync's `error`.
- The learnset default view is defective for two-thirds of species: MovesTab picks the last version group (`champions`, train-only), so 39 of 58 sampled Pokémon open the Moves tab with a 'Lv.' header over 72 rows of '—' and a single 'Train' chip.
- URL state is half-wired: only Dex.tsx uses useSearchParams, only 7 of its 17 controls sync, every write is replace:true, and Reset blanks the query string while leaving view/sort/dir/forms intact — shared links show a different result set than the sender saw.
- Accessibility is effectively absent — zero aria-*, role or tabIndex in the whole src tree; the palette and picker are overlays with no dialog semantics, focus trap or focus return; no :focus-visible, no prefers-reduced-motion, .sr and .skeleton defined and never used, and index.html hardcodes the dark theme.
- Countable rot despite the clean structure: dead exports (MiniStats, Sprite, STAT_KEYS, catchRateApprox, spriteUrl), a dead persisted shiny store slice shadowed by local state, unused CSS, casts that launder unvalidated query params past the type system (Dex.tsx:32-34), and 362 inline style objects against a hand-rolled CSS system.
- Architecture leaves easy wins on the table: caching is in-memory promise dedupe only with no _headers/service worker (a peer in the same field ships both), detail routes scan the 936KB index to resolve a slug, and `npm run data` is manual and absent from build/deploy while public/data is gitignored.

## Standout

The data layer: a resumable, backoff-guarded PokéAPI crawler that emits ~4,892 static shards plus per-collection aggregates and is consumed by a 27-line promise-deduping loader — zero runtime API calls, the complete graph, and correct type/stat/damage math on top of it. It is a shame that a single mis-keyed useEffect in the shared infinite-scroll hook throttles that dataset to 60 rows on the page users open first.
